Garden Cleaner Evolution — teardown

SIMULATOR-GRINDER · Salient Experiences Group · placeId 89907728898683

A leaf-sweeping cleaner with progression through tool evolution. You collect leaves (by clicking leaves), dump them at the Sell Bin for cash, clear each area to 100% — and earn a key + reward and the next, bigger area (Entrance → Shed → Front Yard → Garage → Garden → Tennis Court → Grand Tree…). Cash goes into collection upgrades (Yield/Capacity/Cooldown) and into tool evolution: hands → rake → leaf blower → broom. On top — Rebirth (prestige multipliers, some areas require a rebirth level), quests that grant titles above your head, secret stars and a leaves-collected leaderboard. Built from a full playthrough; the focus is UX and what sets this cleaner apart from its pool neighbors. A case: only ~7K CCU, yet a 97.11% rating.

01Classification — game atoms

What this game is at the mechanics level. A cleaner like its pool neighbors, but with two axes of its own: a key-gated area ladder and a tool evolution over a prestige Rebirth.

Verb
Sweep — collect leaves by clicking (the repeated physical input; the "Try Holding" hint doesn't actually work — you click each leaf); the tool evolves (hands → rake → leaf blower)
Theme
Clean the garden: collect leaves → dump for cash → clear an area to 100% → key and the next area → upgrade the tool → Rebirth
Core systems
Restoration (leaf cleaning) · selling (Sell Bin) · upgrade tree (Grab/Rake/Leafblower) · area ladder (keys) · Rebirth · quests→titles · collection (secret stars) · inventory/capacity
Economy
Cash ($) — from selling leaves (not dollars) · Leaves (the capacity-limited resource) · Lucky Leaves (RNG bonus) · Robux ⬡ (tools, capacity, multipliers)
Mask
Storefront = "clean the garden" (a cleaner); observation confirms and sharpens — progress runs through clearing areas to 100% (a key → a new area) and tool evolution, over a Rebirth prestige and quest-earned titles
Archetype
SIMULATOR-GRINDER — repeat cleaning for capacity, speed and area access; the goal is to become the "ultimate Leaf Sweeper"
Progression
Completion: clear areas to 100% (keys open the next), over Rebirth levels (some areas require a rebirth) as a prestige multiplier. The tool climbs by tiers

03FTUE & UX flow

UX is the focus. Onboarding is extremely explicit: numbered steps (Step 1…7) with arrows walk you through the whole cycle — enter, collect 50, dump, clear, take the key, upgrade, quests.

UX move: a hard-numbered tutorial. Seven arrowed steps (enter → collect 50 → dump → clear → key → upgrade → quests) walk a newcomer through the whole loop in a couple of minutes, and each step ends in a visible reward (cash, bonus, key, title). Sub-areas and goals are highlighted, so you can't get lost. By the end of the FTUE the player has run the full "collect → sell → clear → upgrade" cycle.

04Loop: collect → dump → clear the area

The base loop is simple and tangible: gather leaves to capacity, dump them at the bin for cash, bring the area to 100%. Each step gives immediate feedback.

The loop is deliberately short and "tidy": collect → dump → the area gets cleaner, and area progress (0→100%) is always in view. The key limit is capacity (how much you carry per run), so the first upgrades go into it and into Yield (leaves per pickup). Unlike the dig pool, where you extract random loot, the space here is fixed and finite — the area must be brought to 100%, and it feels like real cleaning.

05Area ladder: keys & rewards

The main progression axis is areas. Each gates by a key (or a Rebirth level), gives its own reward for 100% and holds more leaves than the last. That's the difference from cleaner neighbors.

The area ladder is what turns simple sweeping into progression. Areas rise in volume (Entrance 50 → Shed 500 → Front Yard 1.5K → Garden 2.5K → Tennis Court 4K…) and open via keys for 100% of the previous, with late ones gated by Rebirth level. An area's reward — a key, a price multiplier (1.5x Leaf Price) or speed — means clearing an area always grants both access and an economic boost. That's the core difference from Wash the House (one house) and Dig & Clean (random digging).

06Tool evolution

The second difference — the "Evolution" in the title: the tool climbs by tiers (hands → rake → leaf blower → broom), each with its own upgrades. You pick the tool at the top of the screen.

Tool evolution is the second power axis on top of collection upgrades. Hands → rake → leaf blower → broom — each next tier collects faster and by area, and each has its own branch (Rake: Speed/Range/Width; Leafblower: cooldown/radius/range). A tool can be unlocked by grind OR straight for Robux (Permanent Rake/Leafblower, Early versions) — that's one of the main monetization hooks. The title's "Evolution" is literally about this tool growth.

07Collection upgrades — the cash sink

Cash goes into upgrade stations: collection (Yield/Capacity/Cooldown) and the tool branches. Everything scales in price; the first upgrade is cheap/free — a hook into the hub.

UpgradePrice (cash, start)What it gives
Grab · Yield$20 → …more leaves per pickup
Grab · Capacity$30 → $75 → $150 → $400carry more leaves per run
Grab · Cooldown$75 → …less delay between pickups
Rake · Speed / Range / Width$100 / $120 / $150faster / farther / wider rake grab
Leafblower · cooldown/radius/rangeby tierarea leaf-blowing

Collection upgrades don't change the goal (clear the area) — they compress time: Yield and Capacity speed one run, Cooldown the collection tempo, the Rake/Leafblower branches the area. All scale geometrically, so cash always has somewhere to go. The cheap first upgrade (Yield $20) leads the player into the hub and shows the link "cleared more → upgrade → clean even faster".

08Quests, titles & secret stars

A meta layer over cleaning: quests grant TITLES above your head, hidden stars are a separate collection, and a leaderboard measures leaves collected.

The meta layer gives goals over base cleaning and public status without a badge funnel. Quests (play N days, clear N areas, collect N leaves, max upgrades, find stars) grant titles worn above your head — cheap but visible status. Secret stars are a separate "hidden" collection for exploring areas, and the leaves-collected leaderboard gives a long competitive axis. All of it holds the player once the base cycle is learned.

09Rebirth & prestige

A long layer: the "Fountain of Rebirth" resets progress for prestige multipliers, and some late areas explicitly require a Rebirth level.

Rebirth is a prestige loop over completion: you reset progress and gain permanent multipliers (Reward/Upgrade multiplier, Capacity, Lucky Chance, Speed), and some late areas open only at a Rebirth level (Tennis Court — Rebirth 25). That ties the area ladder to prestige: to go further on the map, you must rebirth and grow stronger. A classic "for months" retention move: re-run the garden faster and with boosts.

10Economy & prices

Few currencies, a closed loop: cash comes only from selling leaves and goes into upgrades and tools. Below — what the price marks show.

AxisWhat the frames showRole
Leaf price~$1/leaf + Lucky Bonus (e.g. +$54 for 50); the Shed gives 1.5x Leaf Pricecash inflow
Capacity (Leaves)50 → 250 → 1K → … (per-run limit)gate on run volume
Grab upgradesYield $20 · Capacity $30 → $400 · Cooldown $75faster collection
Rake upgradesSpeed $100 · Range $120 · Width $150rake area/speed
Area rewardskeys · 1.5x Leaf Price · +0.5/+1 Move Speedaccess + boosts
Rebirthprestige multipliers; late areas require a levellong progress gate

The economy is simple and honest: cash is only earned by cleaning and only spent on speeding up cleaning — a closed loop with no market. Multipliers stack in layers: leaf price (area rewards like 1.5x Leaf Price) × capacity/yield (upgrades) × tool (tier) × Rebirth (prestige). Over the recording the balance reached a few thousand $ and tens of leaves per dump — fast, readable progress. The formula depth belongs to the dig leader; here the economy is deliberately light.

11Monetization

They sell whatever speeds up cleaning: the tools and their upgrades (permanently), capacity, cash/sell multipliers, quick actions. Plus a donation board.

SKUPriceWhat it gives
Permanent Leafblower / Rake⬡399 / 299unlock the tool instantly (grind bypass)
Early Leafblower / Rake⬡49 / 39early access to the tool
Tool upgrades (permanent)⬡39–49Grab Yield/Speed, Rake Area, Leafblower radius/range…
2x Capacity / Infinite 5 min⬡349 / 79x2 capacity / temporarily unlimited
2x Cash / 2x Sell / 10x Lucky⬡299 / 299 / 199income and luck multipliers
VIP / Starter Pack⬡349 / 19skins + 1.5x Sell/Capacity / a starter set
Quick Sell / Quick Upgrade⬡49 / 49instant sell and upgrade

Monetization is entirely about speeding up cleaning. The most characteristic layer is selling the tools and their upgrades permanently: the better tool (Rake/Leafblower/Broom) and each of its upgrades can be unlocked instantly for Robux instead of grinding — a direct purchase of the "evolution". Plus capacity (2x/Infinite — the run bottleneck), multipliers (2x Cash/Sell, 10x Lucky) and Quick Sell/Upgrade (routine speed). Separately, a donation board (Donate 25…2500) as a social feature. Many SKUs, but all hit one pain — cleaning speed.

12HUD & menus

The HUD holds all status (area, %, Leaves, Cash, Lucky, tool), and the menus sit at the screen edges. Below — the distinct families; repeats are omitted.

Navigation is flat: the whole cleaning flow reads off the HUD (area + %, Leaves, Cash, Lucky, active tool), and the meta screens sit at the edges (Quests, Titles, Stats, Settings, Mystery Shop) and via world objects (the Sell Bin, upgrade stations, the Rake Shop, the Fountain of Rebirth). The key UX detail — the area progress X/target (%) is always in view: the player always knows how far to the key.

13Retention

Many return hooks: a daily "3 days in a row" quest, the area ladder and Rebirth as long goals, titles, secret stars, a leaderboard and frequent updates.

Return is held by several layers: a daily quest "3 days in a row" (a direct daily hook), the area ladder and Rebirth as long goals, titles and secret stars as a status collection, a leaderboard by leaves and frequent updates (many dates in the CCU series). Plus the donation board and a Community Server for Codes add a social layer. It's this stack, not peak CCU, that explains a 97.11% rating at ~7K CCU.

14Badges

No badges — status lives in titles (from quests), secret stars and the leaderboard, not in a badge funnel.

The game has 0 badges. Public status is held by titles above the head (Aspiring Sweeper, Handy Helper, Grab Master, Stargazer…), hidden secret stars and a leaderboard by leaves collected. For a fresh cleaner that's deliberate: goals are built into the progression (areas, rebirth, titles), not spun off into a separate achievement list.

15Sound, VFX & ceremonies

The "juice" here is a calm sweeping process with pronounced reward ceremonies (key/area cleared/star). Below — from the captured moment and playthrough observations.

Sweeping: a soft, sustained rustle

The sweeping sound is a soft, sustained "rustle/whoosh" (a gentle attack, almost no peaks): a meditative background you hear constantly and that doesn't tire. It's deliberately dry and looping — cheap feedback on 99% of the time in game.

Reward ceremonies — the pronounced points

InteractionVisualSound / characterPurpose
Sweepingleaves swept in a batcha soft sustained rustle (background)cheap background feedback
Dumping at the binleaves fly off, +$ and Lucky Bonusa coin "ding" + bonus stingera micro-reward per run
Area cleared"YOU UNLOCKED: …" + Claima completion chorda milestone ceremony (key/boost)
Secret star"You Found a Secret Star!"a bright short accenta reward for exploring
Rebirththe Fountain of Rebirth, multipliersan expressive prestige stingerthe main meta ceremony

What to take: sound works for the meditativeness of the routine (a steady sweep rustle) and saves brightness for the reward ceremonies — a dump with a Lucky Bonus, "area cleared", a found star, a rebirth. Those points deliver the dose of satisfaction and mark progress. Ration brightness to the milestones, and keep the background cleaning calm and pleasant — comfort for a many-hour grind.

18What to take

Concrete decisions from a fresh cleaner (10.2M visits, 97.11% rating) that set it apart from its pool neighbors and port into your own project.

1

A key-gated area ladder as the progression axis

Clear an area to 100% → a key → the next, bigger one. Simple cleaning becomes a progression with a visible map, and area rewards (a key, 1.5x price, speed) give both access and an economic boost.

2

Tool evolution as a second power axis

Hands → rake → leaf blower → broom, each with its own upgrade branch. Tool tiers give a sense of growth beyond numbers and become the main monetization hook (Permanent/Early tools).

3

A numbered tutorial with a reward at every step

Step 1…7 with arrows walk through the whole cycle, and each step ends in a visible reward (cash, a key, a title). A newcomer runs the full loop in a couple of minutes and gets the point.

4

Titles from quests instead of badges

Quests grant titles above the head (Aspiring Sweeper, Stargazer). Cheap but visible public status built into the progression, not spun off into a separate achievement list.

5

Rebirth woven into the map

Late areas require a Rebirth level — prestige isn't a separate button but a condition to go further into the garden. It ties the completion ladder to a prestige loop for months.

6

Sell speed, not possibility

Tools and upgrades come by grind OR straight for Robux; capacity, 2x cash, quick actions are accelerators. The paid path is only faster, not exclusive — which is why the rating is high (97.11%).

7

A closed cleaning economy

Cash is only earned by cleaning and only spent on speeding it up — a simple honest loop with no market. Multipliers stack in layers (leaf price × capacity × tool × Rebirth).

8

Depth holds a loyal core

~7K CCU, but 97.11% and 10.2M visits: the area ladder, evolution, rebirth and titles hold a small devoted base. Like Make a Drill Farm — a bet on depth, not on peak CCU.
